rubric.note: Subjective internal editorial ratings with evidence; not an automatic humour metric or an independent live review.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That pause of yours made everyone listen. I'll use a longer one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was a cough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An authoritative cough. Mine will be deliberate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't need to copy me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say that again. I like the certainty.

card.title: Power Looks Good
card.instruction: Act fascinated by confident behavior; imitate it closely while resenting how naturally it seems to work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You got the table just by raising an eyebrow. Must be nice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could ask the waiter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. I'm developing a stronger eyebrow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's coming over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Watch mine outperform yours.

card.title: Power Looks Good
card.instruction: Act fascinated by confident behavior; imitate it closely while resenting how naturally it seems to work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've rung my old headteacher's bell. Why is nobody lining up?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: This is your retirement lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lunch still benefits from orderly pupils.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're your former colleagues.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you should require less supervision.

card.title: Formerly Important
card.instruction: Carry the habits and expectations of a role that once made you important, even when the present no longer supports them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring the shop takings to me, as usual.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You sold the shop last year.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I kept the counting tray.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That doesn't make you the owner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why does the money still fit?

card.title: Formerly Important
card.instruction: Carry the habits and expectations of a role that once made you important, even when the present no longer supports them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's my first lunch order as supervisor. Is soup too indecisive?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's just lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's what a confident supervisor would say.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Order what you like.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you witness that instruction before I risk the soup?

card.title: One Mistake from Gone
card.instruction: Treat every decision as a test of whether you still deserve your place.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've signed the delivery form. Was my signature managerial enough?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It just needs to be legible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So they've lowered the standard for me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: No, it's the same form.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll practise until I deserve the same form.

card.title: One Mistake from Gone
card.instruction: Treat every decision as a test of whether you still deserve your place.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can borrow my car if I approve every stop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm visiting my sister.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A safe first destination. Send me the return plan.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't I decide that?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not while enjoying my comprehensive support package.

card.title: Protection Has Terms
card.instruction: Treat safety, support, and reassurance as arrangements that require you to remain in control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll back your exhibition, provided I choose the guest list.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's controlling the exhibition.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Protecting it from unsuitable viewers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's about independence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let me make independence safe for you.

card.title: Protection Has Terms
card.instruction: Treat safety, support, and reassurance as arrangements that require you to remain in control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The mayor said hello. Should I join her table now?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She says hello to everybody.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then she'll recognise me when you introduce us properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She doesn't know your name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. There's still room for a memorable introduction.

card.title: Chosen by Power
card.instruction: Seek the attention of whoever seems influential and treat that attention as proof that you belong.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put me beside the director in the group photo.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She only asked you to hold her coat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A position of trust.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's taking it back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then photograph the handover. It shows we work closely.

card.title: Chosen by Power
card.instruction: Seek the attention of whoever seems influential and treat that attention as proof that you belong.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you for your lovely private note. Which microphone will you repeat it into?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant it just for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I received it. Now we can broaden distribution.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a staff lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. A captive audience for the full title.

card.title: Public Respect
card.instruction: Seek visible signs of respect and treat private appreciation as insufficient.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you use 'Chair' when introducing me at the picnic?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone knows you're in charge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it won't confuse them to hear it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're passing sandwiches.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Pass them through the Chair.

card.title: Public Respect
card.instruction: Seek visible signs of respect and treat private appreciation as insufficient.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your request for a teaspoon must go through the kitchen supervisor.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're standing beside the teaspoons.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Physical proximity is not authority.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm the kitchen supervisor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then countersign your request. I'll pass it up to catering.

card.title: Chain of Command
card.instruction: Treat every question, favor, and decision as something that must travel through the proper hierarchy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I lend you this ladder, your department head must ask mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're neighbours, cleaning our gutters.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll need to establish departmental boundaries.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I just borrow it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not while the gutter committee remains unformed.

card.title: Chain of Command
card.instruction: Treat every question, favor, and decision as something that must travel through the proper hierarchy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nobody's chairing this picnic. We can't open the hamper.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can decide together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Who authorises together?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just pass the bread.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Is that a nomination? I accept.

card.title: Power Vacuum
card.instruction: Treat any uncertainty about who is in charge as an emergency that must be resolved immediately.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The manager's left early. Who's responsible for the kettle?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Anyone can make tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An uncontrolled beverage structure.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll make it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Say it clearly so we have a chain of succession.

card.title: Power Vacuum
card.instruction: Treat any uncertainty about who is in charge as an emergency that must be resolved immediately.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've given me the broken printer. I'll need authority over purchasing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It probably just needs paper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll oversee paper policy too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a small repair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. A manageable beginning for my department.

card.title: Opportunity for Influence
card.instruction: Find a path to greater influence in every assignment, setback, or unexpected responsibility.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My proposal failed? Then I'll chair the review.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're not forming a committee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Someone must coordinate the absence of one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're getting more work, not more power.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll need a deputy.

card.title: Opportunity for Influence
card.instruction: Find a path to greater influence in every assignment, setback, or unexpected responsibility.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely ribbon-cutting speech. Who has the key to the building?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The chief executive is over there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Does she have the key?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The caretaker does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then my congratulations can wait. I need the caretaker.

card.title: Who Can Authorize This?
card.instruction: Treat titles and speeches as secondary; focus on who can grant access, allocate resources, and create consequences.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your title's impressive. Can you release the repair funds?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My deputy handles finance.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then may I speak to the powerful part of this office?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I make the big decisions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Decide to introduce me to the cheque book.

card.title: Who Can Authorize This?
card.instruction: Treat titles and speeches as secondary; focus on who can grant access, allocate resources, and create consequences.

transfer.action: I copy your commanding pause while presenting {prop}.
transfer.opening: Interesting way to hold the room. Watch mine. {request}
transfer.response: I think my version carries more weight. {counter}
transfer.closing: And gave the method an opportunity to serve stronger leadership.

transfer.action: I ring the bell from my former office beside {prop}.
transfer.opening: This used to come to my desk first. {request}
transfer.response: The title changed, not my judgement. {counter}
transfer.challenge: You don't hold that office now.
transfer.closing: The bell has remained admirably consistent about where it points.

transfer.action: I erase my first answer beside {prop} and hesitate over the pen.
transfer.opening: This needs to prove they chose me correctly. {request}
transfer.response: I'd rather check once than lose the chair over it. {counter}
transfer.closing: Small enough for a mistake to look entirely my fault.

transfer.action: I offer {prop} while retaining the safety key.
transfer.response: I can support the choice once I approve the risk. {counter}
transfer.challenge: Can I have help without your control?
transfer.closing: I'd be worried about the quality of unaccompanied protection.

transfer.action: I position {prop} beside the grandest nameplate.
transfer.opening: An introduction from you would change things. {request}
transfer.response: Make sure they know I was personally invited. {counter}
transfer.closing: Yes, but some invitations sound much closer to the centre.

transfer.action: I move {prop} and the private thank-you note beside the microphone.
transfer.opening: That's lovely; say it where the room can hear. {request}
transfer.response: Private respect deserves a public voice. {counter}
transfer.closing: A clear sentence at a naturally impressive volume will do.

transfer.action: I slide {prop} up the duty chart toward the chair's name.
transfer.opening: This should come from the person above me. {request}
transfer.response: The proper chain hasn't completed its part yet. {counter}
transfer.challenge: Can't you deal with it yourself?
transfer.closing: Not while the arrow still points to an authorized person above me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You’re the headteacher. You should tell the parents I lost the class hamster.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You’re its teacher. You tell them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can supply the facts. Bad news should come from a senior position.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. I’ll appoint you deputy head for the meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My first recommendation is that we hear from the headteacher.

bespokePairs.seedUse: Uses procedural routing from S67-single-a and the delegated bad-news opening from D101-single-a. The school and lost hamster are a new illustrative setting, not inherited source facts. B promotes A to remove the stated obstacle; A uses that promotion to route the same difficult announcement upward again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're the eldest. You tell Mum I think it's time to sell her house.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're twins. You're forty seconds younger. Tell her yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll submit the proposal to you, and you can raise it with Mum.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I reject the proposal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She'll want to know what you've rejected. Could you start with that?

bespokePairs.seedUse: Retains the house-sale and delegated first word from D101-single-b, and procedural routing from S67-single-b. Twins and the forty-second seniority gap are new illustrative details. B exercises the authority A invoked; A uses the rejection as another reason for B to begin.

card.instruction: Treat every question, favor, and decision as something that must travel through the proper hierarchy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your request for a teaspoon must go through the kitchen supervisor.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're standing beside the teaspoons.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Physical proximity is not authority.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm the kitchen supervisor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then countersign your request. I'll pass it up to catering.

card.title: Start the Hard Part
card.instruction: Get someone else to explain, announce, or begin the emotionally difficult part.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You tell the choir the tour's cancelled. I'll hand out the refund forms.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're the organiser.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. The forms will need my full attention.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They'll ask why.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say 'funding' first. I'll join after the disappointed silence.

card.title: Chain of Command
card.instruction: Treat every question, favor, and decision as something that must travel through the proper hierarchy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I lend you this ladder, your department head must ask mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're neighbours, cleaning our gutters.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll need to establish departmental boundaries.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I just borrow it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not while the gutter committee remains unformed.

card.title: Start the Hard Part
card.instruction: Get someone else to explain, announce, or begin the emotionally difficult part.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you phone Mum and begin the conversation about selling the house?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She asked to speak to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll take over once you've said the word selling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the difficult word.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. I'll handle the words that come after it.

transfer.action: I put a responsible-person box beside {prop}.
transfer.opening: We cannot leave that box empty. {request}
transfer.response: Someone must occupy the deciding chair. {counter}
transfer.closing: Who signs the decision made by all?

transfer.action: I add {prop} to a growing list of responsibilities.
transfer.opening: Excellent, another problem that needs my authority. {request}
transfer.response: This connection gives me a wider remit. {counter}
transfer.closing: Not if the new difficulty can still happen outside my boundary.

transfer.action: I put a requisition beside {prop}, ignoring the ceremonial banner.
transfer.opening: Lovely title. Who actually releases the funds? {request}
transfer.response: Show me the signature that opens the door. {counter}
transfer.closing: Did the speech unlock anything we can use?
